Note that we can rewrite this integral as

$$
\int \frac{10\,\text{d}x}{|20x|\sqrt{(20x)^{2}-1}}=10\int \frac{\text{d}x}{|20x|\sqrt{(20x)^{2}-1}}.
$$

This integral now resembles the basic one for $\text{arcsec},$

$$
\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\text{d}u=\text{arcsec}(u)+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of $u$ as the variable, we have $20x.$

So, let's substitute $u=20x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=20\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{20}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}10\int \frac{1}{|20x|\sqrt{(20x)^{2}-1}}\text{d}x & =10\int \frac{1}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}}\cdot (\frac{1}{20}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{|u|\sqrt{{u}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\text{arcsec }u+C \\  & =\frac{\text{arcsec}(20x)}{2}+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
